findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` while retaining the original 5-argument `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` earlier in the same file; Ruby's last-definition-wins silently replaces the 5-arg version, so every existing caller of `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height)` elsewhere in the codebase now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 4 for 5... i.e., 5 given, 3..4 expected). Any pre-existing call site that downsizes with separate width and height arguments (avatar/thumbnail generation paths that call downsize with four+ args) crashes with ArgumentError at runtime, breaking avatar and optimized-image generation that this diff did not intend to touch.

[BUG] `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` passes a percentage string as `dimensions`, but `downsize_instructions` parses the dimensions argument as `WxH` (it does `dimensions.split("x")` and computes an aspect ratio from width and height), so "80%" yields no height and the instruction-building code produces a malformed command or raises, making `convert_with` return false on every iteration. The shrink loop never reduces the file size; it runs 5 failed ImageMagick invocations and then calls `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized tempfile, so the user gets a generic upload failure instead of the promised automatic downsizing — the feature is inert.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop has no failure signal: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when ImageMagick exits non-zero, and the loop ignores the return value, and after 5 iterations the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for` regardless of whether the file is now within `max_image_size_kb`. Users uploading images that cannot be compressed below the limit (e.g., already-small-dimension but high-entropy images, or animated GIFs when `allow_animated_thumbnails` handling fails) wait through 5 wasted ImageMagick subprocess runs and then get the raw size-limit error anyway, having burned server CPU per upload attempt.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop reads `tempfile.size` on every iteration but ImageMagick was launched on `tempfile.path` via a shell backtick; the check is fine, but `allow_animated_thumbnails` is passed for all image types while `optimize` only honors `_animated` instructions when the source path matches `/\.GIF$/i`, so the option is dead weight for PNG/JPEG and misleading to readers. Future maintainers auditing downsizing behavior will believe animated-PNG or other formats get animation-preserving handling via this flag; a subsequent change relying on that assumption alters thumbnail semantics incorrectly.

[BUG] The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is a Ruby method redefinition that silently replaces the first `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, so the four-argument (width, height) signature is dead code. Every existing out-of-diff caller that invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height)` (thumbnail/postamble generation paths) now passes `height` as the `opts` hash and `width` alone as the dimensions string, producing geometry like "100" instead of "100x100" and raising TypeError when `opts[:allow_animation]` is called on an Integer — all thumbnail generation for posts breaks.

[BUG] The downsize loop destructively rewrites tempfile.path in place and ignores the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` (which is `false` when convert fails), so a failed ImageMagick run still proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with corrupted or unshrunk bytes. When ImageMagick fails mid-write (e.g. truncated input or corrupt EXIF), the user's original image is destroyed and the upload either fails with a confusing validation error or stores a corrupt file; there is no fallback to the original data.

[BUG] The client-side check hardcodes 10MB for every upload type (`max_' + type + '_size_kb` was replaced), but the server only auto-downsizes images, so non-image types now bypass the configured limit client-side and are rejected server-side. A user uploading an 8MB attachment (avatar, video, or any non-image) on a site with `max_attachment_size_kb` set to 4096 passes the client check, uploads the full payload, then hits the server-side 413/error — a worse UX than before and bandwidth wasted; admins' per-type size settings are silently ignored by the client.

[BUG] The 413 error handler hardcodes 10MB regardless of which upload type failed, reporting a wrong limit in the error message. When a non-image attachment exceeds its (smaller) server limit, the user is told the limit is 10MB and retries the same file, hitting the same 413 repeatedly — misleading error with no path to resolution.

[BUG] The fixed loop of 5 iterations at 80% is not guaranteed to bring the file under `max_image_size_kb`; `FileHelper.is_image?` returns true for PNGs whose re-encoded size may not shrink proportionally, and no post-loop size check exists. A large high-entropy PNG (e.g. a 9MB screenshot with a 1MB site limit: area shrinks ~10x but PNG re-encode of dense content may stay above 1MB) still passes the loop, and `Upload.create_for` receives an oversized file that then fails validation — the user gets the generic file_too_large error after 5 expensive ImageMagick invocations on the request thread.

[ADVISORY] The refactor changed `resize` to format "#{width}x#{height}" itself while `downsize`'s signature was inverted to take a preformatted string, leaving the two sibling methods with inconsistent calling conventions and no tests in this diff covering either path. The next contributor adding a downsize call site will pass width/height following the resize convention and silently hit the redefinition bug; there are zero spec files in this diff verifying the new dimensions-string contract or the upload downsize loop, so a regression in thumbnail geometry or the 80% loop ships undetected.

[ADVISORY] Animated GIFs are run through `downsize` with `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`, but each of up to 5 loop iterations re-encodes the animation and `convert_with`'s 30-minute-animated path is invoked synchronously on the upload request. A user uploading a 10MB animated GIF on a site with a 1MB image limit triggers 5 sequential full-frame ImageMagick re-encodes inside the HTTP request, blocking a web worker for tens of seconds and causing request timeouts; the sibling flag `allow_animated_avatars`/`animated_image_size` limits are not consulted at all.

[ADVISORY] `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` hardcodes the API download cap at 10MB, ignoring `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` and decoupling the server-side limit from admin configuration entirely. Admins who raise `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB find API URL-based image uploads silently capped at 10MB, and the previously-configurable limit is no longer honored anywhere in this code path.

[BUG] The client-side size check replaces the per-type SiteSetting lookup with a hardcoded 10MB for ALL upload types, not just images. The PR's intent is auto-downsizing large images, but this change silently disables max_avatar_size_kb and any other max_<type>_size_kb client enforcement — users upload 10MB avatars/attachments that pass client validation and are then rejected server-side, converting a friendly pre-upload message into a server error.

[BUG] The 413 handler hardcodes 10MB as the reported max, decoupled from the actual server setting. When the server rejects a non-image upload above SiteSetting.max_attachment_size_kb (e.g. 1MB), the user is told the limit is 10MB, which is wrong for every type except images; admins who lower max_image_size_kb also get a lying error message.

[BUG] The API URL-download path changes its download limit from the SiteSetting to a hardcoded 10MB for all types, unrelated to image downsizing. API clients downloading non-image files (attachments) larger than the site's configured attachment limit but under 10MB now succeed at download then fail at Upload.create_for, and sites with max_image_size_kb > 10MB lose their configured headroom for URL-based uploads — work not traceable to any requirement in the feature.

[BUG] The diff defines self.downsize twice in the same module body — the second definition (from, to, dimensions) replaces the first (from, to, max_width, max_height). The four-argument downsize(from, to, w, h) used by every existing caller raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments) at runtime; the first definition is dead code and the refactor silently changed the public API of OptimizedImage without updating or auditing existing call sites — this is refactor work bundled into a feature PR, not required by it.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop caps at 5 iterations of an 80% pixel reduction with no check that the byte-size goal was actually met before proceeding to upload creation. For very large images (or PNGs where 80% pixel reduction barely reduces bytes), the loop exits with tempfile.size still above max_image_size_kb and the code proceeds to Upload.create_for anyway, so the upload fails — the 'automatically downsize' promise is only best-effort with no user feedback distinguishing it from the pre-feature failure.

[ADVISORY] The animated-GIF branch requires from =~ /\.GIF$/i, but the new caller passes a tempfile path like 'discourse-upload-image' with no file extension, so animated instructions are never selected for the auto-downsize path. Animated GIFs uploaded above the limit are downsized with the single-frame pipeline, which flattens the animation to a static first frame (or bloats/strips frames), silently destroying user content that allow_animated_thumbnails was meant to preserve.

[BUG] The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the first `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` — Ruby does not support overloading, so the 4-argument-arity signature is silently destroyed. Every existing caller of OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height) (thumbnail generation etc.) now hits the new 2-positional-arg + opts method: height is bound to `opts` (or ArgumentError on arity), so dimensions become a hash/garbage string and every optimized-image generation breaks ("#{hash}x" geometry), failing all thumbnail creation site-wide.

[BUG] The downsize loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) with identical input and output paths, and ImageMagick's convert cannot safely read and write the same file in place. convert either fails (non-zero exit, convert_with returns false and the loop keeps looping on the unchanged file) or produces a truncated/corrupt image; after 5 attempts the still-oversized (or corrupt) tempfile is passed to Upload.create_for, so the advertised auto-downsize never actually works.

[BUG] "80%" is a pixel-dimension geometry, not a file-size target, so the while-condition `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` is not what the operation reduces. Five iterations of 80% scaling shrink dimensions by ~0.33x, which may still leave a PNG/GIF above max_image_size_kb (or needlessly destroy quality on an image already under it — the loop is also entered whenever size exceeds the setting even by 1KB); after the loop the oversized file is uploaded anyway, so users still get file_too_large for the exact case this feature claims to fix.

[ADVISORY] The client hardcodes 10MB (var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024) as the size check, discarding SiteSetting, while the server enforces SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb after downsize — two parallel, now-diverged sources of truth. Operators who set max_image_size_kb above 10MB still see the client reject >10MB files before upload; those who set it below 10MB get the client promising 10MB while non-image types still fail server-side; the i18n error message reports the wrong limit in both directions.

[ADVISORY] The server-side URL-download path replaces SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes with a hardcoded 10.megabytes limit for API downloads. Sites that configured a larger max_image_size_kb can no longer API-upload remote images up to their configured limit — a silent narrowing of the API contract to a magic constant with no setting to raise it.

[ADVISORY] The 413 handler's maxSizeKB is hardcoded to 10MB, but a 413 comes from the web server/nginx client_max_body_size, which is an independently configured limit. The error message tells users the max is 10MB when the actual reverse-proxy limit may be lower or higher, misleading users into retry-looping on files the message claims are acceptable.

[BUG] The class defines `downsize` twice; Ruby keeps the last definition, so the first `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is dead code and the surviving method is `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` with arity 3-4. Every existing caller that invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)` with separate width/height arguments (the previous contract, 4-5 args) now hits the second definition and raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), breaking avatar/thumbnail resizing wherever those callers live.

[BUG] The downsize loop passes the literal string "80%" as the dimensions argument, but the new `optimize` contract (post-refactor) feeds that string into `downsize_instructions`, which builds ImageMagick geometry expecting `WxH`. The percentage geometry is applied to a `downsize` operation whose instruction builder interpolates dimensions into a `WxH`-shaped geometry string; the produced instructions are malformed or ineffective for the intended progressive reduction, so the loop either runs all 5 attempts without shrinking the file or ImageMagick errors, and the upload still fails on size — defeating the feature's stated purpose.

[ADVISORY] The animation-preserving branch is gated on `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but the tempfile path here is `discourse-upload-<type>` (no `.gif` extension), so the animated-GIF branch in `optimize` can never trigger on this new call path. Animated GIFs above the size limit get run through the non-animated downsize instructions (which take only the first frame or use `-resize` without `coalesce`), silently destroying animation on uploads the setting `allow_animated_thumbnails` was meant to preserve; users uploading animated images get a frozen single frame.

[ADVISORY] The loop downsizes the tempfile in place (`tempfile.path, tempfile.path`) and then passes `tempfile.size` to `Upload.create_for`, but if ImageMagick fails (convert_with returns false) or the file shrinks below the limit mid-loop, there is no error handling or post-check. When `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false (convert failure, e.g. unsupported/corrupt image), the loop silently burns all 5 attempts and the original oversized file is passed to `Upload.create_for`, producing either the same old 'file too large' error after a multi-second blocking convert loop, or a zero-byte/corrupted tempfile being recorded as an upload.

[ADVISORY] The client-side max size check was changed from the site-setting-driven `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024`, silently changing the accepted constraint without any human acceptance of the new constant. Sites configured with max_image_size_kb above 10MB now have clients rejecting uploads the server would accept, and sites configured below 10MB have clients accepting uploads the server then rejects; the operator's configured intent is silently overridden and the file_too_large message reports a number unrelated to their setting.

[ADVISORY] The API download path also replaced the site-setting cap `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with a hardcoded `10.megabytes`, so the download-size guard and the actual stored limit now come from different sources. For sites with max_image_size_kb set below 10MB, the API URL-download path will fetch images up to 10MB, then the downsize loop compresses them into range — so the effective limit for API URL uploads becomes 10MB regardless of the admin's setting, an unaccepted change in enforcement semantics; conversely no setting can raise the download cap above 10MB.

[ADVISORY] The client-side upload size limit is hardcoded to 10MB, silently discarding the admin-configured SiteSetting.max_<type>_size_kb for every attachment type. Admins who set a smaller limit (e.g. 2MB) still see users prompted with a 10MB allowance for non-image types (avatars, attachments), and admins who raise it above 10MB see uploads rejected client-side with a wrong error message; the actual server policy is now invisible to both operators and users.

[ADVISORY] The 413 error handler hardcodes the limit to 10MB, so the error message shown after a server rejection states a size that no longer matches the server's enforced limit. Users who hit the real server limit (the SiteSetting, which can be lower) are told the max is 10MB, retry, and fail again — a confusing support burden for admins of sites with smaller configured limits.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop's gate is filename-extension-only (FileHelper.is_image?(filename)), so a user who renames arbitrary non-image data to .png or .jpg reaches OptimizedImage.downsize with bytes that ImageMagick/convert cannot process; convert fails (exitstatus != 0, output discarded), tempfile.size never shrinks, and after 5 wasted attempts the oversized file is passed to Upload.create_for anyway. An attacker (or any user) can upload non-image payloads up to the framework's raw request cap labeled as .png; the loop burns 5 sequential convert subprocess invocations per request, a per-request CPU/process amplification (5 shell-outs) triggerable at will, and any size enforcement that relied on max_image_size_kb is bypassed for files that fail to downsize.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop mutates tempfile.path in place and gives up after 5 attempts even when the file still exceeds SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, with no check that the target size was actually achieved before calling Upload.create_for. Files that resist shrinking (already-compressed JPEGs at '80%' five times, or corrupt data) are uploaded over the configured limit, so the admin-configured max_image_size_kb is not a guaranteed invariant — the setting becomes a best-effort hint rather than a hard cap.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedImage.downsize is called with the string '80%' as dimensions, and inside optimize the animated-GIF branch is selected by matching the source path against /\.GIF$/i — but the tempfile is named 'discourse-upload-<type>', which never matches, so animated GIFs larger than the limit are downsampled with the non-animated instruction path. Users uploading oversized animated GIFs get frames-flattened or broken output instead of the animated-aware processing the allow_animated_thumbnails option was meant to select, producing corrupted uploads on a path this diff added.

[BUG] The class defines self.downsize twice — the second definition (from, to, dimensions) completely replaces the first (from, to, max_width, max_height), so any existing caller invoking downsize(from, to, width, height) with four dimension arguments raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). Every pre-existing call site of OptimizedImage.downsize that passes width and height as separate arguments (the signature the first definition was written for, which this diff itself keeps at lines 145-147) crashes with ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments under the redefined method, breaking thumbnail generation for those paths.

[ADVISORY] The downsize retry loop caps at 5 attempts with a fixed "80%" geometry and never verifies the file actually shrank below max_image_size_kb before proceeding to Upload.create_for. Users uploading images that don't compress below the limit after 5 iterations (e.g. large PNGs with high entropy, where 80% area scaling barely reduces bytes) still hit the generic upload-too-large failure — after burning 5 synchronous ImageMagick invocations per request — so the advertised 'automatically downsize large images' behavior silently fails for them.

[ADVISORY] The allow_animation branch in optimize() is keyed on `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but the from path here is the tempfile whose name is 'discourse-upload-{type}' (from FileHelper.download) or the Rails tempfile basename, which never ends in .GIF, so allow_animated_thumbnails can never take effect on this path. Animated GIF uploads are always run through the static (non-animated) downsize instructions, which flattens the animation to a single frame even when the admin has enabled animated thumbnails; the new allow_animation option passed at this call site is dead.

[ADVISORY] The client-side limit is hardcoded to 10MB (10 * 1024) while the server's actual acceptance threshold is now the dynamic SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb (with server-side downsizing above it), so the two ends enforce different limits. Admins who raise max_image_size_kb above 10MB get client-side rejections ('file too large, max 10240 KB') for files the server would now accept, and the I18n message reports a hardcoded 10240 that no longer matches any configured limit; the 413 handler repeats the same hardcoded value.

[BUG] `def self.downsize` is defined twice in the same module body, so the two-argument dimensions form (lines 145-147) silently overwrites the width/height form (lines 141-143) at class-load time. All existing call sites that invoke `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (the signature every current thumbnail generation path uses) now bind `dimensions=max_width` and `opts=max_height` (a plain Integer, not a Hash), producing geometry strings like `"300"` instead of `"300x300"` and an Integer where a Hash is expected — thumbnail generation crashes or produces wrong-sized images for every optimized image after deploy.

[BUG] The downsize loop writes the output to the same path as the input (`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`), destructively overwriting the user's original uploaded file in place with no backup, and the loop gives up after 5 attempts regardless. The original full-resolution image is permanently lost; if 5 iterations of 80% still exceed max_image_size_kb, the (now repeatedly recompressed, quality-degraded) file is passed to Upload.create_for anyway and either rejected or stored mangled; the original bytes can never be recovered since the temp file was the only copy.

[BUG] The loop ignores the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize, and convert_with returns false when the ImageMagick exit status is non-zero. When convert fails (corrupt image, unsupported format), the loop spins 5 times against a possibly truncated/zeroed tempfile (in-place overwrite aborted mid-write), then passes the damaged file to Upload.create_for — a user uploading a valid image gets a broken upload stored or an opaque error, with the original already destroyed in place.

[ADVISORY] `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is called with `filename` before it is guaranteed non-nil on every code path in `create_upload`, and a non-String argument raises NoMethodError inside the begin block. Non-image uploads where the API/URL branch produced a nil filename, or any path where filename is blank, hit `nil.include?` and the request 500s instead of proceeding to normal upload handling.

[BUG] `def self.downsize` is defined twice in the same class body, so the second definition (from, to, dimensions, opts) silently overrides the first, and every existing caller that passes (max_width, max_height) as separate positional args now binds `dimensions = max_width` and `opts = max_height`. Any in-tree or plugin caller invoking OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 500, 300) gets dimensions="500" and opts=300; the constructed ImageMagick geometry becomes "500x" (or the opts hash is replaced by an Integer, raising NoMethodError when opts[:allow_animation] is read), so thumbnail generation breaks or crashes on images that previously resized fine.

[BUG] The downsizing while-loop ignores the boolean return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (convert_with returns false when ImageMagick exits non-zero, with output discarded to /dev/null), so a failed conversion is indistinguishable from a successful one that didn't shrink enough, and the loop just burns all 5 attempts. When ImageMagick fails on a user's image (corrupt file, unsupported format, missing binary), the controller silently proceeds to Upload.create_for with the original oversized (or half-written) tempfile; the user gets either an opaque 500/validation error with no hint that downsizing failed, or an upload of a file that was never actually validated against max_image_size_kb.

[BUG] Passing "80%" as the `dimensions` argument to downsize feeds a percentage into code paths that previously received/produced a "WxH" geometry string; downsize_instructions splits on 'x' and rebuilds the geometry, producing a malformed argument like "80%x" so ImageMagick rejects it every iteration. The automatic downsizing never succeeds at all — every one of the 5 attempts fails with a non-zero exit status that is discarded, and large image uploads fall through to Upload.create_for still oversized, contradicting the feature's entire purpose with zero log or user-visible error.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedImage.downsize is called in-place with from == to (tempfile.path for both arguments), and ImageMagick `convert` reading and writing the same path can truncate or corrupt the source file when the operation fails partway. A user whose image hits a convert failure mid-operation gets their tempfile destroyed (zero-byte or truncated), and the subsequent Upload.create_for either errors cryptically or stores a corrupt upload; writing to a distinct output path and moving on success would make the operation atomic.

[ADVISORY] The client-side max size is hard-coded to 10MB, discarding the site setting, while the server still enforces SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb — but only for files where FileHelper.is_image?(filename) is true. A user uploading a non-image file whose extension happens to pass the filename check, or any case where the server-side downsize loop fails to get the file under max_image_size_kb within 5 attempts (80%^5 ≈ 33% reduction), passes the client gate and then hits a server rejection whose message quotes SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb — a limit the client just told them didn't apply; the two gates now disagree.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The downsize loop's gate is filename-extension-only (FileHelper.is_image?(filename)), so a user who renames arbitrary non-image data to .png or .jpg reaches OptimizedImage.downsize with bytes that ImageMagick/convert cannot process; convert fails (exitstatus != 0, output discarded), tempfile.size never shrinks, and after 5 wasted attempts the oversized file is passed to Upload.create_for anyway. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The downsize loop mutates tempfile.path in place and gives up after 5 attempts even when the file still exceeds SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, with no check that the target size was actually achieved before calling Upload.create_for. adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb a new loop downsizes the same tempfile in place up to 5 times while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, but after the loop it unconditionally calls `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` with no final guard if the file is still over the limit. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] OptimizedImage.downsize is called in-place with from == to (tempfile.path for both arguments), and ImageMagick `convert` reading and writing the same path can truncate or corrupt the source file when the operation fails partway. A user whose image hits a convert failure mid-operation gets their tempfile destroyed (zero-byte or truncated), and the subsequent Upload.create_for either errors cryptically or stores a corrupt upload; writing to a distinct output path and moving on success would make the operation atomic.
